newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks off lows but soft in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks off lows but soft in morning trade.

text.p: U.S. stocks moved above opening lows but remained soft in morning trade on Tuesday, watching a lower bond market after the second quarter employment cost index came in as forecast.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which eked out small gains on Monday, was down around seven points at 8,114 as investors took some profits.
The Nasdaq composite was down 0.72 points at 1563.
The long bond lost 10/32 to yield 6.43 percent, after the Labor Department said the second quarter employment cost index rose 0.8 percent compared with a previous 0.6 percent gain.

"Stocks are a little spooked by bonds here," Chris Dickerson, an analyst at Global Market Strategists said. "The employment cost index came as forecast but the uptick could indicate a reversal of the trend. It is not enough to upset markets but it gives an excuse to take profits."
Stocks and bonds made stunning gains last week after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave an upbeat testimony on the economy to Congress. Dickerson said both were due to take a slight pause.
